nodes.name: dsDNA self-assembled monolayer formation
nodes.procedure: A 10 μL drop of a freshly prepared dsDNA sample (a mixture of 40 μM thiol-modified DNA and 60 μM c-DNA in 10 mM PBS/150 mM NaCl/100 mM MgCl2, pH 7) was placed onto the clean gold electrode surface, covered with a lid and left overnight under the lid at 4 °C. The DNA-modified electrodes were then rinsed with 10 mM PBS/150 mM NaCl, pH 7.

nodes.name: Gold electrode cleaning and polishing
nodes.procedure: Gold electrodes were first cleaned in 0.5 M NaOH by cycling electrode potential between -0.4 and -1.6 V (10 cycles, 0.05 V s-1) and then polished on a microcloth pad in 1 μm diamond and then 0.1 μm alumina slurries, followed by washing with water and ultrasonication in ethanol for 10 min. After that the electrodes were rinsed with water and electrochemically polished in 1 M H2SO4 (from -0.3 to 1.7 V, 10 cycles, 0.3 V s-1) and 1 M H2SO4/10 mM KCl (from 0 to 1.7 V, 10 cycles, 0.3 V s-1). The electrodes were then thoroughly rinsed with Milli-Q water and kept in absolute ethanol for 30 min before DNA immobilisation.

nodes.description: DNA surface coverage determination via RuHex chronocoulometry
nodes.source_text: The DNA surface coverage was estimated... through the analysis of the amount of RuHex electrostatically attracted to the negatively charged sugar-phosphate backbone of DNA... chronocoulometrically by comparing the chronocoulometric signal (step potential from +0.1 to -0.45 V, pulse period of 0.5 s) in 10 mM PBS, pH 7.0, in the absence and in the presence of 0.2 mM RuHex.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cyclic voltammetry of RuHex electrostatically interacting with dsDNA on gold electrodes shows surface-confined peaks at ~−0.27 V with linear ip vs v dependence, confirming surface-confined ET. Laviron analysis gives ks values 35-202 s⁻¹ depending on DNA coverage.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the linear I–v dependence is characteristic of a surface process... the characteristic Laviron trumpet plots were constructed by plotting the values of the voltammetric Epeak versus the log ν

nodes.characterization_summary: Square wave voltammetry (8-1024 Hz) shows surface-confined RuHex signals clearly resolved at f>90 Hz. Komorsky-Lovric-Lovric analysis gives higher ks values (83-321 s⁻¹) than CV/Laviron, with ks decreasing from 321 s⁻¹ at ΓDNA=3.0 pmol cm⁻² to 83 s⁻¹ at 6.1 pmol cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Square wave voltammograms corresponding to surface-confined redox couples... ks = ωmax fmax where fmax is the critical frequency, at which the (I/f) relation... is maximal

nodes.characterization_summary: Chronocoulometry (step +0.1 to −0.45 V) quantifies DNA surface coverage ΓDNA (3.0-6.1 pmol cm⁻²) via stoichiometric RuHex binding to DNA backbone (ΓDNA = ΓRuHex × z/m).
